adult-senior.h1: Adult & Senior Eye Exams in Fort Worth
adult-senior.intro: A thorough, unhurried exam — vision, eye health, retinal imaging and refraction — with every finding explained as we go.
adult-senior.what: Your vision changes as you age. A Pack exam covers vision assessment, eye health evaluation, digital retinal imaging (Optomap) and refraction — and takes the time it takes, up to a full hour.
who: Adults due for an annual exam
Seniors 60+ (annual exams recommended)
Anyone noticing blur, glare or night-driving trouble
Patients who want findings explained, not rushed
expect: Before: bring insurance card, medication list and current glasses
During: full testing with findings explained as we go
After: a clear plan, your prescription, and referrals if a specialist is needed
Seniors: 10% discount on frames & sunglasses
acc: What we test for
Cataracts · Glaucoma · Macular degeneration · Diabetic retinopathy · Dry eye · Refractive errors — caught early, when treatment works best.

childrens.h1: Children's Eye Exams in Fort Worth
childrens.intro: 80% of learning is visual — and 1 in 4 school-age children has a vision problem. Gentle exams, honest answers, and a kids' plan that covers breakages.
childrens.what: We follow the AOA schedule: first exam at 6–12 months, again at 3–5 years, then annually before 1st grade and every year after. We test visual acuity, eye alignment, tracking & focusing, colour vision, depth perception and eye health.
who: Babies 6–12 months (first check)
Children 3–5 and school-age, annually
Kids who squint, sit close, lose their place reading or rub their eyes
Families who want myopia control options
expect: A patient, gentle exam at your child's pace
Clear report of what we found and what it means
Packs Unlimited: $99/year — unlimited exams, $25 frame & lens sets, $25 replacements, same-day pickup
Myopia management: Ortho-K, atropine, multifocal contacts and MiSight; vision therapy referrals
acc: Signs to book sooner
Squinting · Headaches · Sitting close to the TV · Losing place while reading · Rubbing eyes · Avoiding reading.

diabetic.h1: Diabetic Eye Exams in Fort Worth
diabetic.intro: Diabetes can quietly damage the retina. An annual dilated exam catches changes while they're still manageable — and we share the report with your care team.
diabetic.what: Diabetes can cause diabetic retinopathy, diabetic macular edema, cataracts and glaucoma. Retinopathy is a leading cause of vision loss in adults 20–74, progressing from mild non-proliferative stages to proliferative disease.
who: Type 1 & type 2 diabetes — annually
Longer diabetes duration or blood sugar / BP concerns
Pregnancy with diabetes
High cholesterol alongside diabetes
expect: Annual dilated exam with digital retinal imaging and OCT
Staging explained in plain language
Report shared with your primary care doctor / endocrinologist
Risk plan: blood sugar, BP and cholesterol control; don't smoke
acc: Why annual matters
Early retinopathy has no symptoms. The exam is the warning system — by the time vision changes, damage is harder to reverse.

contacts.h1: Contact Lens Exams & Fittings in Fort Worth
contacts.intro: A contact lens prescription is different from a glasses prescription. Precise fitting, trial lenses and training — daily, toric, multifocal, scleral and Ortho-K.
contacts.what: Your fitting includes corneal measurement & curvature, tear film assessment, lifestyle assessment, trial lenses and a follow-up — plus insertion/removal training if you're new to contacts.
who: New wearers who want proper training
Astigmatism (toric) or presbyopia (multifocal)
Keratoconus or severe dry eye (scleral)
Kids/teens for Ortho-K myopia control
expect: Measurements, tear-film check and trial lenses
Care rules: hygiene first, never sleep in lenses unless prescribed, replace on schedule
Brands: Alcon, Acuvue, Bausch + Lomb, CooperVision and more
Reorder online anytime via Order Contacts (top of this site)
acc: Lens types
Daily disposable · Bi-weekly / monthly · Toric · Multifocal · RGP · Scleral · Specialty / Ortho-K overnight myopia control.

dry-eye.eye: Dry Eye Clinic · Center of Excellence
dry-eye.h1: Dry Eye Therapy in Fort Worth — a Center of Excellence
dry-eye.intro: Dry, irritated, tired eyes have a cause — and over 30 million Americans share it. We diagnose the type first, then treat the glands, not just the symptoms.
dry-eye.what: Tears are made of oil, water and mucus. Dry eye is either Aqueous Deficiency (not enough tears) or Evaporative (tears evaporate too fast) — most commonly from Meibomian Gland Dysfunction (MGD), plus blepharitis and rosacea. Causes include screens, aging, air conditioning, contacts and hormones.
who: Burning, gritty or watering eyes
Blur that clears when you blink
Drops that stopped working
Post-cataract dry eye
expect: Diagnosis: LipiView, LipiScan, MMP-9 / InflammaDry, tear osmolarity, Schirmer's test, meibography
Our 4-step MGD plan: 1) IPL Therapy (4 sessions) 2) Radiofrequency 3) Manual Expression 4) Regener-Eyes
Other options: BlephEx, lid hygiene, warm compresses, punctal plugs, prescription drops (Restasis, Xiidra, Cequa, Tyrvaya)
Honest guidance — treatment only if it will genuinely help
acc: Not sure it's dry eye?
Take the 60-second Dry Eye Quiz in the Patient Centre — five questions, scored instantly, with a plain verdict.

ipl.h1: IPL Treatment for Dry Eye — OptimaMAX
ipl.intro: The next generation of dry eye relief: InMode OptimaMAX combines IPL + RF to calm inflammation and restart oil flow — with a photofacial bonus for the skin around your eyes.
ipl.what: Intense pulsed light targets the inflammation driving dry eye and the abnormal blood vessels around the glands. Light pulses reduce inflammation, address Demodex/bacteria contributors and warm blocked glands so oil flows again. Radiofrequency stimulates meibum, improves tear quality, tightens skin and softens fine lines.
who: Evaporative dry eye / MGD
Rosacea-related dry eye
Patients whose drops no longer help
Anyone wanting the skin benefits too: spots, redness, uneven tone
expect: Preparation: consultation, skin assessment, protective eyewear, cooling gel
Treatment: gentle pulses around the lids, ~10–15 minutes
After: mild redness fades in hours; typically ~4 sessions spaced weeks apart
Photofacial bonus: age spots / sun damage, rosacea, acne, uneven skin tone
acc: IPL vs drops
Drops replace tears for a few minutes. IPL treats why the tears fail — the inflamed, blocked glands — so relief compounds across sessions.

emergency.h1: Emergency Eye Care in Fort Worth
emergency.intro: Eye injuries, chemical exposure, sudden vision loss, flashes & floaters, pain or infection — call immediately. Same-day appointments, walk-ins welcome.
emergency.what: We treat corneal abrasions, foreign bodies, infections (pink eye), uveitis / iritis, retinal detachment symptoms and subconjunctival hemorrhage. Don't rub the eye, don't remove embedded objects, and flush chemicals with water for 15 minutes while you call.
who: Sudden vision loss or a curtain over vision
Severe eye pain or trauma
Flashes, new floaters or bleeding
Chemical splash or something stuck in the eye
expect: Call 817-831-6141 first — we prioritise emergencies Mon–Thu
Same-day appointments and walk-ins when something can't wait
If we're closed (Fri–Sun) and it's severe: urgent care or ER, and ask them to contact us
acc: First aid while you call
Don't rub · Don't remove embedded objects · Flush chemicals 15 minutes with clean water · Bring any chemical container or object details with you.

digital-strain.h1: Digital Eye Strain Relief in Fort Worth
digital-strain.intro: Prolonged screens, reduced blinking, blue light and poor ergonomics strain your eyes. Children over 3 hours a day on screens are at higher risk.
digital-strain.what: Symptoms: dry eyes, headaches, strained eyes, blurry vision, neck & shoulder pain. Most cases improve with setup changes — persistent strain deserves an exam to rule out prescription or focusing problems.
who: Screen-heavy jobs and students
Kids on screens 3+ hours a day
Headaches that build through the workday
Blur after long screen sessions
expect: Ergonomics: screen 4–5 inches below eye level, 20–28 inches away
Display settings and lighting adjusted to your space
The 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds
Blue-light glasses can help — we'll tell you honestly if they're worth it for you
acc: Still strained after fixes?
Book an eye exam — uncorrected prescription and focusing issues hide behind 'screen strain' more often than people expect.

eye-disease.h1: Eye Disease Diagnosis & Management in Fort Worth
eye-disease.intro: Early detection saves sight. Glaucoma, cataracts and macular degeneration are diagnosed, staged and managed here — with specialist co-management when you need it.
eye-disease.what: Glaucoma (open-angle, angle-closure, normal-tension, congenital, secondary) is diagnosed with pressure, visual field and optic nerve imaging and treated with drops, laser or surgery referral. Cataracts cause foggy vision, night difficulty, halos and faded colours; surgery is timed to when vision interferes with daily life. Macular degeneration (dry vs wet AMD) shows as blurry central vision and wavy lines; AREDS vitamins help dry AMD, anti-VEGF injections treat wet AMD via specialists.
who: Family history of glaucoma or AMD
Age, diabetes, high eye pressure or steroid use
Foggy vision, halos or night-driving trouble
Straight lines looking wavy, or dark central spots
expect: Pressure, visual field and optic nerve imaging for glaucoma
Cataract assessment and honest surgery timing
AMD monitoring with imaging; specialist co-management
Prevention guidance: UV protection, no smoking, healthy diet
acc: Risk factors at a glance
Glaucoma: age, family history, ethnicity, high eye pressure, diabetes, steroid use. Cataracts: age, diabetes, smoking, UV, steroids. AMD: age, family history, smoking.

laser.h1: Laser Eye Surgery Consultation in Fort Worth
laser.intro: Considering LASIK, PRK or SMILE? Start here: candidacy, measurements and honest advice — then pre-op and post-op co-management back at Pack.
laser.what: Candidates are 18+, with a stable prescription and healthy corneas. LASIK creates a flap and reshapes the cornea with a quick recovery. PRK is surface ablation with no flap and a longer recovery — often better for thin corneas. SMILE is also discussed at consultation.
who: 18+ with a stable prescription
Tired of glasses or contacts
Thin corneas (PRK may suit better)
Anyone wanting the full risks picture first
expect: Consultation and measurements here at Pack
Surgeon referral for the procedure itself
Pre-op and post-op co-management back at Pack
Risks covered honestly: dry eye, halos and glare are possible; most patients achieve 20/20
acc: Co-management, explained
Your optometrist handles consultation, measurements and pre/post-op care while the surgeon performs the procedure — one team, start to finish.

POSTS.t: Cataract Awareness Month: Understanding This Common Condition
POSTS.s: June is Cataract Awareness Month. Reading getting harder, night driving worse? Those can be early cataract signs — what cataracts are, how they progress, and why an exam now beats guessing.

POSTS.t: Why Do I Have Wrinkles Under My Eyes?
POSTS.s: Under-eye wrinkles appear for many reasons — aging, sun exposure and thin skin. What actually helps: skincare, microneedling and Morpheus8, explained without the sales pitch.

POSTS.t: Can Dry Eye Cause Blurry Vision?
POSTS.s: Yes — an unstable tear film blurs the image before it reaches your brain. How we test with Schirmer, tear breakup time and a gland check.

POSTS.t: Can Radiofrequency Tighten Loose Skin?
POSTS.s: RF tightens loose skin on face, neck and jawline as a non-surgical alternative — and dry eye patients often notice fewer fine lines after RF treatment.

POSTS.t: What is IPL & RF Treatment for Dry Eye?
POSTS.s: Lumecca IPL reduces inflammation; Forma-I RF melts blocked gland oil. What a session feels like step by step — and why ~4 sessions are typical.

POSTS.t: How Often Should You Have an Eye Exam?
POSTS.s: Adults and seniors: every year. Children: once between 3 and 5, then annually once school starts. The AOA schedule and the symptoms that mean do not wait.

POSTS.t: What Are Specialty Contact Lenses?
POSTS.s: Scleral, RGP, hybrid and custom lenses for keratoconus, severe dry eye and hard-to-fit prescriptions — when standard soft lenses are not enough.

POSTS.t: Does Ortho-K Work for Nearsightedness?
POSTS.s: Orthokeratology lenses are worn overnight to gently reshape the cornea — clear daytime vision without glasses, and slower myopia progression in children.

POSTS.t: How Do You Know If You Have Binocular Vision Dysfunction?
POSTS.s: When the eyes do not team up properly: headaches, dizziness, reading fatigue and double vision can follow. How BVD is tested and treated.

POSTS.t: How Learning-Related Vision Problems Affect Reading Skills in Children
POSTS.s: 80% of learning is visual. Tracking, focusing and eye-teaming problems can look like reading or attention problems. (Sep 2024 edition.)

POSTS.t: Does Glaucoma Always Need Treatment?
POSTS.s: Glaucoma damage cannot be undone, only slowed — which is why early detection at a routine exam matters. When monitoring is enough and when treatment starts.

POSTS.t: What is the Management of Myopia?
POSTS.s: Myopia control today goes beyond stronger glasses: Ortho-K, atropine and multifocal contacts can slow progression in kids. (Jul 2024 edition.)

POSTS.t: August Brings Contact Lens Health Week
POSTS.s: Healthy habits for lens wearers: hygiene, replacement schedules, and why you should never sleep in lenses unless prescribed.

POSTS.t: Why Am I Seeing Spots and Squiggly Lines?
POSTS.s: Spots and squiggly lines are usually floaters — debris in the vitreous gel. When floaters signal a retinal tear instead, and why new floaters need a prompt exam.

POSTS.t: Can Orthokeratology Improve Eyesight?
POSTS.s: Ortho-K reshapes the cornea overnight — a safe, non-surgical alternative to LASIK for myopia, hyperopia and astigmatism.

POSTS.t: Does Vision Therapy Work for Concussion?
POSTS.s: After a concussion, focusing, tracking and eye teaming often suffer. How vision therapy supports recovery and when to ask for a referral.

POSTS.t: Why Is a Comprehensive Eye Exam Important?
POSTS.s: A comprehensive exam checks far more than a glasses prescription — it can catch glaucoma, diabetes and even cardiovascular signs early.

POSTS.t: How Do I Know If My Child Needs Vision Therapy?
POSTS.s: Trouble staying on task, sloppy handwriting, losing place while reading — overlooked vision problems can look like classroom struggles. (May 2024 edition.)

POSTS.t: Are Eye Floaters a Big Deal?
POSTS.s: Usually harmless, occasionally urgent. The difference between ordinary floaters and the flashes-and-curtain pattern that means same-day care.

POSTS.t: Vision Rehabilitation for Stroke Recovery: How Does It Work?
POSTS.s: Vision problems are common after stroke and can slow every other part of recovery. How rehabilitation assessment and therapy help.

POSTS.t: Who Is Most at Risk of Getting Cataracts?
POSTS.s: Cataracts affect around 25% of people who live to 80+. Risk factors: age, family history, diabetes, smoking, UV exposure, steroids and obesity.

POSTS.t: How Do I Know If My Dry Eyes Are Severe?
POSTS.s: Daily burning, watering and drops that stop working are severity signals. How we grade dry eye and when in-office treatment (IPL/RF) replaces drops.

POSTS.t: What Is Done in Vision Therapy?
POSTS.s: Guided exercises and activities that retrain how the eyes and brain work together — what a typical therapy program involves.

POSTS.t: What Are Early Warning Signs of Macular Degeneration?
POSTS.s: Blurry central vision, straight lines looking wavy, dark spots. Dry vs wet AMD and why early signs deserve a prompt dilated exam.

POSTS.t: When Should I Be Worried About Eye Allergies?
POSTS.s: Itching and watering are usually allergies — until they are not. The symptoms that separate seasonal allergies from infection or something more serious.

POSTS.t: Can Dry Eyes Be Serious?
POSTS.s: Untreated dry eye can damage the cornea and raise infection risk. When 'just dry eyes' deserves real treatment. (Jun 2024 edition.)

POSTS.t: How Vision Problems Can Interfere With Stroke Recovery
POSTS.s: Reading, balance and rehab exercises all depend on vision. Addressing visual deficits early supports the whole recovery. (Jun 2024 edition.)

POSTS.t: How Does LASIK Co-Management Work?
POSTS.s: Your optometrist handles consultation, measurements and pre/post-op care while the surgeon performs LASIK. (Jan 2024 edition.)

POSTS.t: Is Poor Eyesight More Common in Women?
POSTS.s: Women live longer and face higher risk of several eye conditions — the reasons, and the screening habits that protect vision.

POSTS.t: What Eye Condition Is Considered an Eye Emergency?
POSTS.s: Eye pain, flashes/floaters, infection, sudden vision changes, chemical exposure — the emergencies that need immediate care, and what to do first.

POSTS.t: Early Warning Signs of Diabetic Retinopathy You Shouldn't Ignore
POSTS.s: Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of blindness in adults — and its earliest signs are easy to miss. Annual dilated exams catch it while it is still manageable.

POSTS.t: What is the Management of Myopia? — 2024 Update
POSTS.s: An updated look at myopia management for Fort Worth families — Ortho-K, atropine and multifocal options compared.

POSTS.t: Can Dry Eyes Be Serious? — Signs Checklist
POSTS.s: A checklist edition: the specific symptoms that move dry eye from nuisance to condition needing in-office care. (Mar 2024 edition.)

POSTS.t: How Do You Know If Your Child Needs Vision Therapy?
POSTS.s: Poor visual skills can make school success harder — classroom signs of overlooked vision problems and how vision therapy helps. (Mar 2024 edition.)

POSTS.t: How Does LASIK Co-Management Work? — Patient Guide
POSTS.s: A patient-guide edition walking through each co-management step, from first consultation to final post-op check. (Oct 2023 edition.)

POSTS.s: The parent-focused edition: how learning-related vision problems show up in reading homework, and what an evaluation covers. (Oct 2023 edition.)

POSTS.s: Sleep in Ortho-K lenses, see clearly all day without glasses — how overnight corneal reshaping works and who it suits.

POSTS.t: Vision Problems & Stroke Recovery — Overview
POSTS.s: An overview edition on vision's role in stroke rehabilitation — and why a vision assessment belongs in the recovery plan. (Aug 2023 edition.)

POSTS.s: Screen-heavy jobs strain eyes: ergonomics, the 20-20-20 rule and protective eyewear — a workplace eye wellness primer.

INS.vsp: Good news — VSP is one of our most common plans. It typically covers your exam with a copay and gives a frame/lens allowance in our boutique. Bring your card (or member ID) and we will verify exact benefits before your exam.
INS.eyemed: Yes — we work with EyeMed. It usually covers exams and provides a frame allowance; designer frames above the allowance are priced as the difference, told to you up front.
INS.bcbs: Yes — Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas is accepted, particularly valuable for medical eye care: diabetic exams, glaucoma checks and urgent visits are often billed medically. Bring both your medical card and any separate vision card.
INS.aetna: Yes — Aetna plans are accepted. Coverage varies between medical and vision riders, so email a photo of your card to office@packoptical.com and we will confirm before you book.
INS.cigna: Yes — Cigna is accepted. Bring your card and the team will verify benefits before any treatment. For diabetic eye checks, medical coverage often applies.
INS.cec: Yes — Community Eye Care is accepted. Bring your member ID and we will verify your exam and frame benefits before your visit.
INS.davis: Yes — Davis Vision is accepted. It typically covers exams and provides a frame allowance in our boutique; we will confirm your exact benefits before you are seen.
INS.medicaid: Yes — Medicaid is accepted for patients ages 20 and under, including children’s exams. Bring the Medicaid card and we will verify coverage before the visit.
INS.superior: Yes — Superior Vision is accepted for exams and eyewear. Bring your card and we will verify your allowance before you choose frames.
INS.tricare: Yes — Tricare is accepted. Coverage depends on your plan and whether the visit is routine or medical; bring your card and we will verify before treatment.
INS.uhc: Yes — United Healthcare is accepted. Many UHC plans separate medical and vision benefits, so bring both cards if you have them and we will confirm exactly what applies.
INS.medicare: Medicare is accepted for medical eye care — including diabetic retinal exams and cataract/glaucoma monitoring. Routine refraction for glasses is treated separately; we will explain exactly what is covered before we start.
INS.other: Very likely — we accept most major plans, and unlisted plans are often still workable. Email a photo of your card to office@packoptical.com or call 817-831-6141 and we will check it for you, free.
INS.none: No problem at all — many med spa clients and second-pair buyers are self-pay. Exam pricing is quoted up front, aesthetics consultations include an exact written quote, and there is never a surprise bill.
